primary.title: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier
primary.author: Napoléon Ier
primary.rationale: The complete collection of Napoleon's correspondence offers direct insight into his thoughts, decisions, and interactions across his military and political career. It is a foundational primary source for his biography and the Napoleonic era.

primary.title: Mémorial de Sainte-Hélène
primary.author: Las Cases, Emmanuel-Auguste-Dieudonné de
primary.rationale: This work records Napoleon's dictations and conversations during his exile on St. Helena. While filtered through Las Cases, it provides Napoleon's own perspective on his life and actions, making it a crucial, albeit subjective, primary source.

primary.title: Maximes et pensées de Napoléon
primary.author: Napoléon Ier
primary.rationale: A collection of Napoleon's aphorisms, maxims, and reflections, offering concise insights into his philosophy, strategic thinking, and views on leadership and human nature.

secondary.title: Napoleon: A Life
secondary.author: Roberts, Andrew
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive and highly regarded modern biography that draws on extensive archival research, offering a detailed and balanced account of Napoleon's life and impact.

secondary.title: Napoleon and Wellington: The Battle of Waterloo and the Great Commanders Who Fought It
secondary.author: Chandler, David G.
secondary.rationale: David Chandler is a preeminent military historian of the Napoleonic era. This book provides in-depth analysis of Napoleon's military campaigns and his ultimate adversary.

secondary.title: The Campaigns of Napoleon
secondary.author: Chandler, David G.
secondary.rationale: Although published slightly before 1976, this remains a seminal and indispensable work for understanding Napoleon's military genius and strategic acumen. It is frequently cited in later scholarship.

suggestions.notes: The 'Mémorial de Sainte-Hélène' is a primary source in that it records Napoleon's own words and thoughts, though it was transcribed and compiled by Emmanuel de Las Cases. The 'Maximes et pensées' are collections of his sayings, often compiled posthumously but directly attributed to him. The inclusion of Chandler's 'The Campaigns of Napoleon' is justified by its enduring status as a foundational scholarly work, despite its pre-1976 publication date.
